violated_contract: A BLE listener coroutine that awaits a caller-supplied async notification callback must surface that callback's exception to the coroutine's own caller. bleak.BleakClient.start_notify detects an async callback and wraps it so every notification runs in its own detached asyncio.create_task (bleak/__init__.py), never awaited by anything the listener itself awaits. sdks/python/omi/ble.py::listen()'s `_handler` awaited `on_packet`'s result inline with no try/except, so a packet-callback exception became an unretrieved task exception logged by asyncio's default handler instead of reaching the coroutine awaiting listen()/listen_payload() -- the caller saw the listener hang, not the real failure.
canonical_prevention: Catch exceptions raised inside the notification handler itself, store the first one, and signal a shared event the listener's poll loop also watches; once that event fires, re-raise the stored exception from the coroutine the caller is actually awaiting, instead of relying on the notification callback's own call frame to propagate it.
